sections.rawHeading: 1 · Licensing (GOV on the state statutes; LOCAL detail partially unverified)
sections.title: State licensing and registration
sections.confidenceNote: on the state statutes; LOCAL detail partially unverified
sections.markdown:
**No statewide license covers chimney work in Kansas, and there is no state contractor board for general construction.** Kansas has **no state general-contractor, residential-builder, or home-improvement license.** Licensing, testing and enforcement happen at the **city and county** level, and chimney masonry, relining and sweeping fall outside any state credential. The big local regimes:
- **Wichita / Sedgwick County:** contractors are licensed through the **Metropolitan Area Building & Construction Dept. (MABCD)**. MABCD tells homeowners to verify roofers are "registered with the State of Kansas and licensed with MABCD." MABCD issues **General Contractor** and **Trade Contractor** licenses; the qualified person must pass an ICC exam ("a score of 75 percent or better"; Kansas Standard ICC exam or an ICC test release) (https://www.sedgwickcounty.org/mabcd/contractor-licensing/ — GOV, Sep 25 2026). No masonry- or chimney-specific class is listed.
- **Johnson County:** runs a county contractor-licensing program (**11 license types**: Class A, B and C general classes — Class C covers "construct, remodel, repair, and demolish single-family or duplex residences" — plus trade classes DE electrical, DF fire protection, DFA fire alarm, DM mechanical, DP plumbing, DR roofing, DS swimming pool, DW wood framing). **There is no masonry or chimney class** (https://www.jocogov.org/department/contractor-licensing/new-license-license-types — GOV, Sep 25 2026). Lookup: https://cls.jocogov.org/searchcontractor. Which cities honor the county license was not confirmed.
- **Wyandotte County / Kansas City, KS:** reported to require only a business license (not re-verified).

*(Exam content for Johnson County classes and which cities participate were not confirmed. See blockers.)*

**The one statewide exception is roofing.** Under the **Kansas Roofing Contractor Registration Act (K.S.A. 50-6,121 to 50-6,138)**, no one may act as a roofing contractor without an **Attorney General registration certificate** (K.S.A. 50-6,123). The application must include:
- a certificate of liability insurance of **not less than $500,000** (K.S.A. 50-6,125);
- proof of workers'-comp coverage or an exemption;
- a Kansas tax clearance.

The AG sets the annual fee by rule, **capped at $500** (K.S.A. 50-6,128). A chimney is not roofing, so chimney work is neither AG-registered nor state-licensed. "Licensed and bonded" here means a county or city credential, valid only in that jurisdiction.

sections.title: What the credential does not test
sections.markdown: Statewide, there is **nothing to verify for chimney work**: no exam, no registry, no bond. County contractor exams (MABCD, Johnson County), where they apply, test general building and permit knowledge, not flue diagnosis or masonry skill. The AG roofing registry is verification-rich but does not touch chimneys. Individual certifications (CSIA CCS, C-DET; NCSG CCP/CCR) and an independent audit fill a total vacuum.

sections.rawHeading: 3 · Home sale (GOV on the narrow statutes; industry-form detail REF/unverified)
sections.title: Seller disclosure when a home sells
sections.confidenceNote: on the narrow statutes; industry-form detail /unverified
sections.markdown:
**Kansas has NO statute requiring a general seller property-condition disclosure form.** Sellers are held to common-law rules against concealing or misrepresenting known material defects. Two narrow *statutory* seller duties do exist, and neither touches the chimney:
- **Special assessments (K.S.A. 12-6a20):** the seller must disclose that the property is subject to a special assessment or fee and get the buyer's written acknowledgment.
- **Radon (K.S.A. 58-3078a):** residential sale contracts must carry the statutory radon notice, and sellers must disclose known elevated radon test results.

In practice most sales use the **Kansas Association of REALTORS® Seller's Property Condition Disclosure Statement**, a voluntary industry form. It reportedly names the fireplace and chimney and asks when they were last cleaned. *(That form's wording was NOT re-verified in this pass. Do not quote it until confirmed.)* Using it is contractual, not statutory. No inspection is mandated at transfer; NFPA 211 Level 2 stays a NATIONAL STANDARD.

sections.title: Consumer remedies and cancellation rights
sections.markdown:
The **Kansas Consumer Protection Act (KCPA), K.S.A. 50-623 et seq.**, bars deceptive and unconscionable acts in consumer transactions. It works on three levels:
- **Public enforcement:** the **AG's Consumer Protection Division** and county or district attorneys can seek civil penalties of **up to $10,000 per violation** (K.S.A. 50-636(a)). A continuing practice counts as a separate violation each day, and willful violation of a court order costs up to $20,000.
- **Private right of action:** a consumer may recover **actual damages or the § 50-636(a) civil penalty, whichever is greater** (K.S.A. 50-634(b)), plus attorney's fees as the Act provides. There are no automatic treble damages.
- **Door-to-door cancellation (K.S.A. 50-640):** a consumer may cancel a door-to-door sale of **$25 or more** "until midnight of the third business day after the day on which the consumer signs an agreement." **Caveat:** the section excludes maintenance or repair visits the buyer requested, unless additional goods or services are sold, and emergency sales with a signed waiver.

Complaints: ag.ks.gov Consumer Protection.

sections.rawHeading: 5 · Permits & codes (medium; genuine patchwork — local editions not verified)
sections.title: Permits and building codes
sections.confidenceNote: medium; genuine patchwork — local editions not verified
sections.markdown: **Kansas has no statewide building code for general residential construction.** Each city or county adopts its own, usually an IRC/IBC edition with local amendments. Wichita/Sedgwick (MABCD), Johnson County jurisdictions, and Kansas City, KS each maintain their own adoptions. **Unincorporated rural counties may have no code and no permit process at all.** Where a building department exists, chimney relines, rebuilds, crowns and solid-fuel appliance installs are generally permit work; routine sweeps and like-for-like caps generally are not. *(Current IRC editions per jurisdiction not confirmed in this pass.)*

sections.rawHeading: 6 · CO law (medium-high — absence supported by the state's own alarm statute, Sep 25 2026)
sections.title: Carbon monoxide and smoke alarm law
sections.confidenceNote: medium-high — absence supported by the state's own alarm statute, Sep 25 2026
sections.markdown: **Kansas appears to have NO statewide residential carbon-monoxide-alarm statute**, meaning no state mandate for rentals, new construction or sale. The state's residential alarm law is the **Smoke Detector Act, K.S.A. 31-160 through 31-164** (K.S.A. 31-160: "shall be known and may be cited as the smoke detector act"). K.S.A. 31-162 requires smoke detectors (one per story in single-family dwellings; hardwired in units built after Jan 1, 1999). **None of the act's sections mentions carbon monoxide** (https://ksrevisor.gov/statutes/chapters/ch31/031_001_0060.html ; https://ksrevisor.gov/statutes/chapters/ch31/031_001_0062.html ; …/031_001_0063.html ; …/031_001_0064.html — GOV). That supports, but cannot by itself prove, the absence of any CO statute elsewhere in the K.S.A. The act's penalty is a fine of up to $25 (K.S.A. 31-163), and it supplements local law (K.S.A. 31-164). CO requirements are **LOCAL**, through adopted building and fire codes. A narrow administrative CO-detector rule for **lodging establishments** with fuel-fired equipment, wood-burning fireplaces or attached garages has been reported (K.A.R. 4-27-8). That covers hotels, not homes. *(The regulation number and text were not re-fetched this pass; label as unconfirmed.)* There is no pre-sale CO certificate. A permitted chimney or solid-fuel job is still the natural moment to add alarms.

sections.title: Solid fuel and environmental rules
sections.markdown: No statewide burn-ban or stove-emission regime. Not a material content section for KS.

sections.title: Scam patterns and enforcement
sections.markdown: The Kansas AG's Consumer Protection Division pursues home-repair and door-to-door contractors. The door-knock "we noticed your chimney" pitch is a textbook K.S.A. 50-640 + KCPA scenario, while a sweep the homeowner requested is excluded from § 50-640. **No KS chimney-sweep-specific enforcement action has been confirmed.** Use patterns, not names.
